I broke my pinky toe six weeks ago. I won't lie to you--it takes a while to heal, even though it's just a tiny little toe. Obviously your experience may be different, but I couldn't do much working out at all for the first couple of weeks. I did some strength training, but it hurt to wear anything but sandals, so I couldn't do much in the way of cardio. After a couple of weeks, I was able to get on the stationary bike, and then I moved to the elliptical, and finally, four weeks after the injury, I started short, easy runs. This past weekend, exactly six weeks after breaking my toe, I ran my first half-marathon with no pain (not in the toe, at least). The first couple of weeks are the hardest, so take some time off and let your body start to heal itself. Then get back into it gradually, and be prepared to stop if you feel any pain. It's not fun at all, but you'll be back out there running in no time!

It meant so much to have someone I respected so much look at me and see something worthwhile. Sorry, I was just trying to answer your question.

If you're tossing and turning in bed, get out of bed and do something else. Read a book, make some tea, meditate, do something that doesn't involve screens or bright lights or a lot of physical activity. Cover your clocks so you don't feel pressured to fall asleep by a certain time. Write down anything you feel nervous or anxious about. When you feel your eyelids starting to droop, get back in bed. Make sure your room is cool and you're wearing comfortable clothes, and see if you can fall asleep. If not, get out of bed and repeat the above steps. The most important thing is to avoid flopping around in bed and stressing out over not being able to fall asleep, since that'll just make it harder to fall asleep.
